curriculum.lesson_evidence: A music showcase gathers your best work: singing, playing or composing. A programme lists the items in order, with the title and the performers. Before each piece, a short introduction tells the audience what to listen for, such as 'This piece uses a crescendo.' Perform with a count-in and finish together. The audience claps at the end. Afterwards, reflect on the elements you used and what you would improve. Always treat every performer with kindness and give feedback as two stars and a wish.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Write a three-item programme for a music showcase and a one-sentence introduction for one item.

FEEDBACK
Strong answer: '1. Round (class), 2. Rain composition (me), 3. Body percussion piece (me and a friend). Introduction: This piece uses a crescendo from soft to loud.' The introduction names an element to listen for.

WATCH FOR
Thinking that you must perform everything you know. A showcase shows a few well-prepared pieces and tells the audience what to listen for.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Prepare a music showcase of three items from this unit for family. Write the programme and an introduction for each item. Perform, then collect two stars and a wish and write a reflection about the elements you used.

Write a short reflection naming one artistic choice you changed and why. Movement or instrument work is optional, adult-supervised and can be described instead.

teach_steps.example:
WORKED MODEL
Example: Lena's programme has three items: 1. Row, Row, Row Your Boat (round, class); 2. Playground (composition, Mina and Ravi); 3. A steel pan listening piece. Before the second item, Mina says, 'Listen for the quick shakers in section A.' The audience listens, claps and gives two stars and a wish.

TRY FIRST
Write a three-item programme for a music showcase and a one-sentence introduction for one item.

FEEDBACK
Strong answer: '1. Round (class), 2. Rain composition (me), 3. Body percussion piece (me and a friend). Introduction: This piece uses a crescendo from soft to loud.' The introduction names an element to listen for.
teach_steps.explain:
A music showcase gathers your best work: singing, playing or composing. A programme lists the items in order, with the title and the performers. Before each piece, a short introduction tells the audience what to listen for, such as 'This piece uses a crescendo.' Perform with a count-in and finish together. The audience claps at the end. Afterwards, reflect on the elements you used and what you would improve. Always treat every performer with kindness and give feedback as two stars and a wish.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner make intentional visual, music, drama or dance choices and name their effect, rather than saying an artwork is simply “nice”. Keep every claim linked to an element or technique.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the elements, techniques or performance choices that carry the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. For movement or instruments, use a clear space, ask an adult to be nearby and stop if anything feels unsafe. You may always describe a choice instead of performing it. One deliberate artistic choice with a named effect is more useful than a longer praise sentence.
